component.name: rfiles
component.summary: Fast file manager with tabs, dual panes and previews

description.p: rfiles is a file manager written in Rust: tabs, dual panes, a column view, DirectLook previews (images, PDFs, video, text, archives), archives as folders, tags, git status, network locations and removable drives.
rfiles began as the Linux port of rustyfiles by Özer Güzel.
The update dot also shows on About in Settings and on the Updates card.
A terminal pane under the file list (F4, or Run command here): your shell in the current folder, following the folders you browse to. Open in terminal still opens your own terminal app.
The Overview page lists network places in their own section and has Home in Quick access. A small dot on Settings shows when an update is available.

Permissions and owner columns, links, templates, select by pattern, paste an image or text as a file, mount disk images, search filters, your own right-click actions, a folder tree, phones and cameras, file servers on the network, folder sharing over Samba, and Open in Disks. The start page is now called Overview, and Home opens your home folder.

Security fixes: opening a git repository can no longer run commands from it, and files opened from archives are no longer readable by other users. Updates are signed. From rustyfiles 0.7.0: extract several archives at once or smartly, tar and split archives, tag search with AND/OR/NOT, more ways to group, and a settings search box.

Search inside files, run commands in a terminal from any folder, use rfiles as the Open/Save dialog of other apps, full-quality camera RAW previews, certificate and program version details, and every text translated in every language.
Error messages and other texts that showed in Turkish whatever the language now follow the chosen language, and Turkish becomes an ordinary translation.

Offline network shares no longer freeze the window and are marked offline, encrypted (LUKS) drives can be unlocked, removable drives get an eject button, copy progress shows on the taskbar icon, and quick search can have a global shortcut through the desktop portal.
rfiles can check for new releases and install them, and the date format is now a pattern you type, with a live preview.
The first release as rfiles (was rustyfiles): Home lists recently used files, dates follow the date setting everywhere, and the app never asks for stars or donations.
